newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans collapse on fund selling, technicals.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans collapse on fund selling, technicals.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures collapsed on Tuesday, battered by aggressive fund selling amid bearish technical signals and indications demand for old crop supplies was waning, pit sources said.

"The only bullish factor is supply tightness in old crop beans and now it appears demand is slowing down which may hold the carryout to 125 million (bushels) or more," said Joel Karlin, vice president of commodities Everen Securities.
"Also there was technical selling. July tried to hold at $8.50 but three times down and pounding on that level finally broke it," Karlin said.

Chartists said a weekly trend line was broken in the July at $8.51 per bushel which prompted aggressive selling. Funds sold an estimated 20 million bushels on the day, pushing July to its lowest level since April 24.
Pit sources said trade was thin and choppy ahead of the midday expiration of the May but when that contract ended lower, sellers jumped in.
"Once the May was off the board and the threat of a squeeze in soymeal was gone, it just fell," a trader said.
Soybeans ended 21 to 2-3/4 cents per bushel lower with July down 21 at $8.45.

Some floor sources said funds had been long and used the technical break as an opportunity to liquidate positions. With little bullish fundamental news to drive the market, buyers were hard to find, traders said.

"These are stale longs," one floor trader said. "We've been going strong for months now. The world was alerted to the fact that we had tight stocks in the January crop report. In the absence of dramatic news, we have nowhere to go."
The active soybean seeding pace further hit new crop values.
USDA on Monday said 46 percent of the U.S. soybean crop was planted as of Sunday, up from the 26 percent average.
On the day, funds sold an estimated 20 million bushels of soybeans. Refco Inc and Dean Witter were said to be featured sellers. Rosenthal Collins sold at least one million bushels July.

In options, Rosenthal Collins sold 900 July $8.50 calls and sold 900 July $8.50 puts at 48 to 46 cents premium. CIS bought 300 July $8.25 puts at 7-1/2 and sold 300 July $7.50 puts at 1/2 cent, traders said.
Soybean futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 64,000 contracts, compared with Monday's actual volume of 59,777.
